summary: Ready-work faults name an observed daemon socket access failure on first claim

replay.detail: No replay or stored identity changes.

schema.detail: Uses existing harness timeline error operations and harness.diagnostic claims; no database or claim schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Failed st work claim Unix connects emit a bounded typed stderr receipt. Native drivers retain the receipt before tool output redaction and bind it to a current ready step, attempt, readiness epoch and runtime incarnation. Codex command exitCode/aggregatedOutput and Claude PostToolUseFailure are now observed. Other failures retain the existing generic readiness diagnostic. Every command using the shared daemon client now skips its configured connection wait or follow retry for OS-reported Unix connect errors other than not-found, connection-refused, interrupted, would-block and timed-out. This includes permission/path errors and resource-pressure failures, where waiting might have helped; advice for immediate failures points to permissions or the socket path. Success output and provider permission policy are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No migration or required seat restart. Newly launched native wrappers can produce the new cause receipt; already-running older wrappers retain their previous behavior until their normal relaunch.

manual.detail: No configuration change. Faults expose the actual endpoint and OS error; operations can inspect the sandbox policy or socket path. This does not override provider policy or automatically retry a denied claim.

recovery.detail: Older builds continue to use the generic readiness diagnostic. Ready work remains ready on a failed claim; once socket access is fixed the seat can claim normally.
